craft_claim: Non-Anglophone civic and devotional traditions practice forward-facing uplift with distinct warrants and proofs, so the inspirational voice cannot be defined by Anglophone convention alone.

supporting_evidence.note: Tagore's song offerings carry devotional longing with a forward, world-facing hope; the collection's English form is the author's own radical rewriting, and won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature.

supporting_evidence.location: Address to the Constituent Assembly, 14-15 August 1947
supporting_evidence.note: Nehru's canonical Indian civic-uplift address names past struggle and poses the future as labour and collective pledge rather than triumph alone.
Marti's Spanish-language civic essay fuses anti-colonial diagnosis with a forward ideal for a continental readership, a formal rhetorical situation rather than a translated Anglophone template.

supporting_evidence.location: Opening address, World's Parliament of Religions, 11 September 1893
supporting_evidence.note: Vivekananda reframes sectarian history into a forward interreligious call, an Indian civic-prophetic uplift performed on an international stage.

counterevidence.note: Section E translation limit: the English Gitanjali is Tagore's own radical rewriting (reordering, omission, fusion) rather than a rendering of the Bengali, and its uplift is not fully recoverable in English; section E also declines a single universal technique because warrants and accepted proofs differ.

scope: Cross-cultural study of the tone; the dossier treats Indian and Latin American cases as load-bearing analysis.
exceptions: The shared family resemblance should not be inflated into a universal formula: warrants differ (sacred, civic, developmental) and so do accepted proofs.
